leads.title: American Samoa Code - Marriage Provisions
leads.documents: Documents legal status of same-sex marriage licensing: code does not specify sex of parties but refers to age of 'the male' and 'the female' and prescribes form identifying parents as 'son' and as 'daughter'.
leads.detail: Cited in article as 'The American Samoa Code' with no URL visible in provided text

leads.title: 1963 Sodomy Law and 1979 Fono Criminal Code Revision (effective 1980)
leads.documents: Documents decriminalization of consensual same-sex sexual activity; 1963 law criminalized male homosexual and heterosexual sodomy, 1979 revision made consensual sodomy legal except public acts, prostitution, minors or mental incapacity; age of consent 16 regardless of gender/orientation.
leads.detail: Cited as 'first criminal law against sodomy was enacted in 1963' and 'In 1979, the Fono revised criminal law... The law took effect in 1980' - no URL visible

leads.title: 2003 Same-Sex Marriage Ban Bill by Rep. Sua Carl Schuster
leads.documents: Documents legislative attempt to ban same-sex marriage to establish territory position and avoid mainland-type lawsuits; voted against by House Judiciary Committee and full Senate.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Representative Sua Carl Schuster introduced legislation to ban same-sex marriage in 2003' - no URL visible

leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges (2015)
leads.documents: Documents uncertain applicability of US Supreme Court same-sex marriage ruling to American Samoa due to U.S. nationals status and unorganized and unincorporated political status.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Obergefell v. Hodges' and 'In July 2015' review; no URL visible in provided text

leads.title: Attorney General Talauega Eleasalo Ale - July 2015 Review Statement
leads.documents: Documents government enforcement review machinery: AG office reviewing Obergefell decision to determine its applicability to American Samoa.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Attorney General Talauega Eleasalo Ale said that his office was reviewing the decision to determine its applicability' - July 2015, no URL visible

leads.title: Governor Lolo Matalasi Moliga - 2015 Non-Applicability Statement
leads.documents: Documents executive position that Supreme Court same-sex marriage ruling does not apply due to preamble, constitution, Christian values and unorganized/unincorporated status; backed by Assemblies of God, Catholic Church, and Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
leads.detail: Cited as Governor Lolo Matalasi Moliga statement a week after AG statement; no URL visible

leads.title: Respect for Marriage Act (117th U.S. Congress, signed 2022)
leads.documents: Documents federal recognition requirement: all territories including American Samoa must recognize though not perform same-sex marriages performed legally elsewhere; requires equal treatment under US federal law since 13 December 2022; signed by President Joe Biden.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Respect for Marriage Act passed by the 117th United States Congress and signed into law by President Joe Biden in 2022' - no URL visible

leads.title: High Court of American Samoa - Birth Certificate Ruling
leads.documents: Documents gender-identity legal status: birth certificates should only be altered to correct information erroneous at time of recordation or to reflect name change due to adoption.
leads.detail: Cited as 'The High Court of American Samoa has held that birth certificates should only be altered...' - no URL visible

leads.title: Office of Vital Statistics - Transgender Birth Certificate Policy
leads.documents: Documents rights machinery for transgender persons: office interprets High Court ruling to cover transgender applications; will change name with name change order, and may change gender marker with medical documentation of sex change.
leads.detail: Cited as 'The Office of Vital Statistics has interpreted this ruling...' - no URL visible

leads.title: Lambda Legal Position and Plaintiff Call (Omar Gonzales-Pagan)
leads.documents: Documents rights-enforcement machinery: argument territories must comply due to supremacy of federal law as individual right/liberty; asks any American Samoan same-sex couple denied license to contact Lambda Legal, ACLU, GLAAD, or National Center for Lesbian Rights.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Omar Gonzales-Pagan of Lambda Legal argued...' and call for contact; no URL visible
